summary: Frontend-only iteration-4 retest on the public UTC-browser URL. The temporal service fixes passed deterministic tests: weather slices from the current hour, IST tide timestamps remain future-only, and a 0.73 m to -0.09 m adjacent-hour change is FALLING. Login, dashboard placement, theme switching, K-01/02/03 cards/details/map popups, DEMO exclusion, metadata markup, no-fake-data check, and one-weather/one-marine request count passed. Critical integration regression: StrictMode aborts that single shared in-flight request, so both real cards, tide timestamps, Analytics environmental chart, alerts, and failure isolation are unavailable at runtime. Analytics also still emitted 6 ResponsiveContainer -1-dimension warnings.

ui_bugs.issue: The K-* detail footer has Weather/Tide attribution and Updated fields, but does not include the explicitly required literal 'Sources:' label. With the fetch regression, Updated renders as — rather than an '... ago' timestamp.

integration_issues.flow: Initial authentic weather/tide load under React StrictMode
integration_issues.issue: A polling cycle now issues exactly one weather and one marine request, but StrictMode's first effect cleanup aborts both. The second mount reuses the same aborted in-flight promises, so both cards remain UNAVAILABLE. Browser logs show net::ERR_ABORTED for both requests. Weather-only and marine-only 500 isolation retests consequently fail because the supposedly independent source is also unavailable.

integration_issues.flow: Analytics environmental chart and Recharts sizing
integration_issues.issue: Environmental Conditions Trend renders WEATHER DATA UNAVAILABLE with no x-axis labels because of the aborted weather request. Opening Analytics still emits 6 ResponsiveContainer width(-1)/height(-1) warnings despite minHeight={200}.

action_items: Fix in-flight dedup cancellation ownership: a StrictMode cleanup must not abort the one shared network operation that the remount reuses. Preserve exactly one request while allowing the second consumer to receive its successful result.
Retest actual UTC-browser Analytics labels and next tide values after live data is restored; service-level temporal tests pass, but runtime verification is blocked.
Fix ResponsiveContainer initial width/height measurement; minHeight alone did not remove the 6 warnings.
Add the literal Sources: footer label to K-* drain Environmental Conditions sections and ensure successful loads show an 'Updated: ... ago' value.
critical_code_review_comments: RCA: weatherService/tideService cache a promise created with the first component mount's AbortSignal. useEnvironment cleanup aborts that signal; the StrictMode remount receives the cached aborted promise instead of live data. Request deduplication therefore reduced network count but broke all environmental runtime data.
App.js is 1,867 lines, well above the 700-line threshold; extract environmental dashboard/detail/analytics/alerts components.
useEnvironment still mounts and starts external API polling before mocked authentication succeeds; environmental traffic is not scoped to the dashboard session.
The env-impact-level data-testid is on the small impact badge, not the Prototype Risk Model container that owns Sources/Updated metadata, reducing selector correctness for the requested footer check.
seed_data_creation: None. Used real public Open-Meteo requests plus temporary Playwright 500 interception; deterministic service tests used local mocked payloads only.
test_credentials: Read /app/memory/test_credentials.md and used the pre-filled mocked BMC-OPS-4091 flow; no real authentication was performed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: First verify a fresh public load has exactly one successful weather and one successful marine request (not net::ERR_ABORTED) and that both source cards show LIVE values. Then in UTC verify six Analytics labels begin at current IST hour, tide high/low humanized values are future/non-zero, and the live trend matches adjacent marine points. Re-run both one-source 500 isolation cases and deterministic high-rain alert badge/source checks. Temporal Jest tests currently pass; runtime checks are blocked only by the abort/dedup integration regression.
rca_of_the_issue: React StrictMode runs setup → cleanup → setup. useEnvironment's first cleanup aborts its controller. Both services stored fetch promises tied to that first signal and return those same promises to the second setup for 5 seconds. Thus there is exactly one request per API, but it is aborted and both consumers receive null. Reproduction: fresh public load in UTC, authenticate, observe both cards UNAVAILABLE and net::ERR_ABORTED logs; network count is one weather plus one marine.
